newsitem.title: USA: Suicide of suspected Versace killer brings relief.
newsitem.headline: Suicide of suspected Versace killer brings relief.

text.p: The suspected killer of designer Gianni Versace committed suicide on board a houseboat just a few miles from the murder scene, "a desperate person with little room to move," Miami Beach's police chief said on Thursday.

The death of Andrew Cunanan on Wednesday in Miami Beach ended what officials called one of the biggest manhunts in U.S. history and brought widespread relief, especially to the area's terrified gay community.
"The reign of terror brought upon us by Andrew Cunanan is over," Police Chief Richard Barreto said after police stormed the houseboat and found the body on the second floor.

Police had named the 27-year-old gay gigolo as the only suspect in the July 15 murder of Versace outside his mansion in glamorous Miami Beach, a crime that shocked the world. He was also wanted for four other murders in a cross-country spree.

Barreto told a later news conference after an autopsy of Cunanan's body: "The medical examiners confirm he died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head ... To date there has been no suicide note or other correspondence from Mr. Cunanan that would relate why he committed the crimes he is accused of."

The suicide weapon, a .40 calibre handgun, the same type used in the Versace murder, was undergoing tests in a police laboratory, Barreto said. The homicide investigation was still considered open as much evidence still had to be processed and many questions were still unanswered, he added.
Barreto said he knew nothing about Cunanan's relationship with the houseboat's owner, how long he had been there, or how long he had been dead when police burst in.
"I think he was a desperate person with very little room to move about either here or elsewhere in the United States, " he said.
Asked about the houseboat's owner, FBI special agent Paul Phillip said: "We'd very much like a chat with him."

Local media have named the owner as Torsten Reineck, a German citizen who also owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. German police said on Thursday they believed Reineck might be a fugitive they had been seeking since 1992.
Cunanan was identified through a thumbprint on his driver's license. They declined to say if the face was so damaged by the gunshot wound that it was unrecognizable.
Nor was there an answer to whether Cunanan was infected with AIDS, which some criminologists have suggested might have fuelled his drive to kill.
"We will never know what motivated Andrew Cunanan to kill but we know he will never kill again," Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas said.

A caretaker's tip-off on Wednesday afternoon led dozens of police and FBI agents to the two-level houseboat on Indian Creek just 40 blocks from the murder site. After a four-hour stand-off, agents lobbed in teargas grenades and stormed the boat, where they discovered the body.

It took hours for police to positively identify the corpse although it was immediately thought to be Cunanan. Before dawn, police fingerprint experts finally made a definite match and Barreto declared: "All across the nation our citizens can stand down and breathe a sigh of relief."

Cunanan was suspected in the murder of four other men all over the country. The killing of Versace, couturier to stars and royalty, plunged the fashion world into mourning. Versace, 50, was cremated in Miami last week and the ashes buried in Italy on Friday.
News of Cunanan's death brought relief to Miami Beach, a mecca for tourists and for gays, who had lived in fear and anxiety while the suspected killer remained on the loose.

"Life can get back to some semblance of normal here," Patric Chemaly, a 27-year-old medical student, said. "I think people were afraid to go out. They were always wondering if the trick (sex partner) they took home was Andrew."

Miami Beach Mayor Seymour Gelber told Reuters: "This is a great relief for the city of Miami Beach. We're accustomed to greeting tourists, not searching out killers ... the last 10 days have been rather dreary."
In Milan, the Versace family said they were relieved and grateful to those who helped to resolve the murder.

FBI agents received hundreds of tips about alleged sightings of Cunanan and as late as Wednesday morning they were investigating reports he had been seen in New Hampshire, only hours from the Canadian border.
In Washington, Attorney General Janet Reno and FBI chief Louis Freeh said his death concluded "one of the most massive fugitive manhunts in American law enforcement history."

Cunanan was on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list of fugitives even before the Versace slaying. He was also wanted for the murders of his former lover Jeffrey Trail, 28, in late April; their mutual friend David Madson, 33, in May; Lee Miglin, 72, also in May, and William Reese, 45, also in May.
